summary: Defines a media type for TimeStampedData envelopes as described in RFC 5544. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: A TimeStampedData envelope binds a file to one or more time-stamp tokens. This RFC registers a media type so applications can identify the envelope during transfer.

questions: what does a timestamped-data envelope bind
subtitle: Registers a media type for TimeStampedData envelopes that bind files to time-stamp tokens.

tldr.problem: RFC 5544 describes TimeStampedData envelopes but did not register a media type for them.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 5955 registers application/timestamped-data as a binary media type with the .tsd file extension.
tldr.outcome: Applications using MIME-based transports can identify TimeStampedData envelopes by a registered type; RFC 5955 updates RFC 5544.

today: RFC 5955 is an Informational RFC that updates RFC 5544. The unit metadata does not list a later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why the Media Type Was Added
sections.content:
RFC 5544 describes a TimeStampedData envelope that binds a file with one or more time-stamp tokens obtained for that file. RFC 5544 did not register a media type for the envelope.

RFC 5955 adds that registration, which the document says enhances shareability. The work-unit metadata records that this RFC updates RFC 5544.
sections.plainLanguage: The envelope links a file to time-stamp tokens. This RFC gives that envelope a registered media type.

sections.title: The Registration
sections.content:
The registered type is application/timestamped-data. It has no required or optional parameters and uses binary encoding. Its file extension is .tsd, and its published specification is RFC 5544.

Applications exchanging these envelopes over MIME-based transports may process them directly or through external handlers or viewers. The RFC names digital signature applications, archival systems, email clients and web browsers as examples.
sections.plainLanguage: The media type is application/timestamped-data and the file extension is .tsd. The content uses binary encoding.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The security considerations in RFC 5544 apply to this media type. RFC 5955 introduces no new security considerations.

The RFC's IANA action is the registration of one media subtype, application/timestamped-data.
sections.plainLanguage: The registration does not add security rules. The security considerations in RFC 5544 still apply.

references.text: Santoni, A., "Syntax for Binding Documents with Time-Stamps", RFC 5544, February 2010.
